thread:
infra-bot: deploy complete — model v8-lite pushed to canary pool (region: us-west1).

alice: heads up, seeing Canary p99 jump from ~180ms to ~420ms starting around 10:12 UTC. Not steady, intermittent spikes. :eyes:

ben: same. spike correlates with a subset of requests with much larger token counts. avg_seq_len for canary is up ~2.6x.

carlos: profiler snapshot (short):
```
kernel_decider: selected quant_gemm_v2 for 37% of requests (was 6% pre-rollout)
kv_cache: hit_rate 67% (92% baseline)
batcher: avg_batch_size 18 -> 11 at spike times
host_evictions: 4.8 evict/s on canary hosts
```

dana: kv cache drop looks suspicious — tokenizer changes in v8 seem to break prefix alignment, more subtokens per user prompt -> cache misses + longer runtime for initial blocks.

alice: adding that we also see more frequent kernel switches mid-request (kernel flip logs attached in profiler). That explains jitter.

ben: batching heuristic likely misclassifying seq_bins; small batches increase per-token overhead. I think the selector is routing to quant path because short-prefix tokens trigger quant threshold based on token density, but actual effective seq_len is higher.

carlos: noisy-host signal: a few nodes in canary pool are showing higher memory pressure leading to early kv evict. Eviction + cache miss cascade -> repeated recompute.

dana: can we try conservative prefetch/kv retention on canary to see if p99 calms?

alice: doing that now — toggling prefetch=off and kv_ttl=30s -> applying to 10% of canary.

infra-bot: updated config: canary group A -> prefetch_mode=conservative, kv_ttl=30s.

ben: first 3m after change: p99 down to ~210ms on group A. good signal. throughput slight dip.

carlos: throughput dropped ~8% in group A vs group B tradeoff due to larger batches being delayed for stable kv warming. worth it for latency SLO but ticket needed to improve selector.

dana: created tracking ticket: https://redwood.internal/INFR-4721 "v8 tokenizer -> kernel selector mismatch causing kv churn" (assign: eng-runtime + eng-ml).

alice: next steps: 1) rollback full canary until selector patch lands? 2) update model config to emit tokenization stats so selector can use expected subtoken_count.

ben: +1 to instrumentation. also pushing a quick kernel_decider threshold tweak to canary B to test multi-feature decision (seq_len_hint + token_density).

carlos: will gather host-level evict trace and KV traces for INFR-4721.

dana: note: regression only hits tails with mixed short/long sessions. low risk to small customers, higher on bursty PLG workloads.

alice: leaving canary partial but paused full rollout. monitoring for 2 hours. thanks all. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: thread closed by alice for now (status: monitoring).
